description: US-citizen children of a removed parent can visit but cannot relocate without giving up their schooling and their mother's work. The household simply operates in two countries.
energy_note: His daughter can visit him. He cannot attend her graduation.

aspect: He becomes a voice on a phone
description: Parenting continues by video call across a time difference, with his authority steadily reduced to money sent and advice given about a place he is no longer in.
energy_note: A father who exists mainly as a screen.

description: Where he was the earner, removal converts a working household into a remittance-dependent one, or into poverty, immediately.
energy_note: One morning, and the household income is gone.

aspect: Trying to return is now a felony
description: Illegal re-entry after removal is a federal criminal offence, so the man who goes back to his children is prosecutable rather than merely removable.
energy_note: Going back to his kids is now a crime with a sentence.

description: His daughter holds the phone too close and shows him her spelling test. He says he is proud. She asks when he is coming. He says soon, which is what he said in March, and she has stopped asking follow-up questions about it.
energy_note: She has stopped asking when, which is worse.
